title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. These notes study the 'structure at infinity' of the moduli stacks M_{g,ν}. The boundary of the Deligne–Mumford compactification is a divisor D with normal crossings in a smooth stack, and the notes build the combinatorial–homotopical data attached to its strata.

Notation, reconstructed from the neighbouring pages:
- D_{d} is the normalized stratum where at least d branches meet. D*_{d} is its open part, where exactly d branches meet.
- D_{Δ_r} = ⨿_{d_0>d_1>…>d_r} D_{d_0,…,d_r}. A point is a point of the d_0-stratum together with a decreasing flag of subsets of its local branches, of cardinalities d_0>d_1>…>d_r.
- P*_{Δ_r} is the punctured tubular neighbourhood (the deleted normal bundle) of D*_{Δ_r}.
- Π_{Δ_r} = Π_1(D*_{Δ_r}) and Π̃_{Δ_r} = Π_1(P*_{Δ_r}) are the corresponding fundamental groupoids.
- Π̃ → Π is an extension by the local system T_{Δ_r}. This is the free abelian 'inertia' group generated by the loops around the d_0 branches.

Previous page. Grothendieck observed that there is no natural map between Π_{d,d'} and Π_{d'}: the open stratum D*_{d,d'} lands in the boundary of D_{d'}, not in D*_{d'}.

This page opens: 'par contre il y en a entre Π_{d,d'} et Π_d', i.e. such maps do exist towards Π_d. He makes this precise as follows.
1. Take a semi-simplicial map α: Δ_r → Δ_{r'} with α(0)=0. This means the base stratum d_0 is kept and only intermediate members of the flag are forgotten.
2. The forgetful map D_{Δ_{r'}} → D_{Δ_r} is then finite étale, because it amounts locally to choosing subsets of a finite set of branches.
3. Hence so is the induced map D*_{Δ_{r'}} → D*_{Δ_r}, being induced over D*_{Δ_r}.
4. The same holds for the punctured tubular neighbourhoods. One gets a 2-cartesian square of groupoids (216): Π̃_{Δ_{r'}} → Π̃_{Δ_r} over Π_{Δ_{r'}} → Π_{Δ_r}.
5. In this square the horizontal maps are finite coverings of groupoids, i.e. injective on π_1 with finite index.

He then remarks that all of this is formal and trivial, valid in any setting, and does not use the specific normal-crossings hypothesis.

The next page introduces the non-formal ingredient. Using the normal-crossings hypothesis, the Π̃_{Δ_r} (not the Π_{Δ_r}!) form a genuine semi-simplicial groupoid, including faces with α(0)≠0. Those faces go from deeper strata to shallower ones through tubular neighbourhoods.

The purpose is to encode the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν}: how the fundamental groupoids of the boundary strata and their punctured neighbourhoods fit together. This is relevant to the Teichmüller tower / Galois action program of the Esquisse.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. Minor caveats: the finite-étale claim for D_{Δ_{r'}} → D_{Δ_r} requires that the flag is of subsets of branches at a fixed d_0-stratum point, with d_0 preserved. This is exactly why α(0)=0 is imposed. For components, 'injective on π_1 of finite index' should be read componentwise (a finite covering of groupoids), as Grothendieck's own parenthetical correction indicates.

ideas.what: Indexing the strata of a normal-crossings divisor by decreasing flags of branch subsets (d_0>…>d_r). This gives semi-simplicial objects D_{Δ_r}, D*_{Δ_r}, P*_{Δ_r}, and the faces with α(0)=0 are finite étale.
ideas.modern_name: Semi-simplicial resolution / nerve of the stratification of a normal crossings (log) divisor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in mixed Hodge theory (Deligne, Hodge II/III) and later log geometry
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the 'structure à l'infini' of M_{g,ν} without such details

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoids of open strata (Π) and of their punctured tubular neighbourhoods (Π̃), with Π̃ an extension of Π by the inertia local system T, forming 2-cartesian squares under the finite étale faces.
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid of the deleted tubular neighbourhood / homotopy link; tangential base points; local monodromy (inertia) extension
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989), Ihara–Nakamura (structure at infinity of moduli), Quinn (homotopy links)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (sketched); SGA1 XIII and Grothendieck–Murre for tame fundamental groups near a normal crossings divisor

missed.claim: This page separates two kinds of data. The finite-étale faces with α(0)=0 are formal and need only Π. The general faces need the tubular neighbourhood groupoids Π̃, which form a semi-simplicial groupoid (next page). That is essentially the exit-path / homotopy-link description of a stratified space, packaged as a semi-simplicial groupoid indexed by flags of strata. Grothendieck aims to apply it to the boundary of M_{g,ν}.
missed.quote: Toutes ces considérations sont de nature essentiellement formelle et triviale
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This anticipates the exodromy / exit-path ∞-category formalism (MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie, Barwick–Glasman–Haine) applied to the Deligne–Mumford boundary. However, this page itself contains only the formal part, and Ihara–Nakamura covered the moduli-specific structure at infinity.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is explicitly the 'formal and trivial' preliminary: finite étale forgetful maps between flag-indexed strata and the resulting 2-cartesian squares of fundamental groupoids. It is correct and well organised but standard. The genuinely interesting non-formal semi-simplicial structure on the Π̃ appears on the next page.
transcription_corrections: First line: 'par contre il y en a entre Π_{d,d'} et Π_d.' (in contrast to the previous page, where there was no natural map Π_{d,d'} → Π_{d'})
'Précisons ce point, en considérant un morphisme' (correct)
'donc aussi D*_{Δ_{r'}} → D*_{Δ_r} (induit au dessus de D*_{Δ_r}) d'où un diagramme 2-cartésien' — probable reading
'où les flèches horizontales induisent sur les π_1 des injections d'indice fini (en fait disons que Π_{Δ_{r'}} → Π_{Δ_r} fait de Π_{Δ_{r'}} un rev. fini de Π_{Δ_r})'

'Toutes ces considérations sont de nature essentiellement formelle et triviale, et valables dans un cadre quelconque; [n'utilisent pas] l'hypothèse spécifique des croisements normaux' — 'croisements normaux' rather than 'coïncidences'
Marginal note roughly: 'Ceci montre que les Π̃_{Δ_{r'}} → Π̃_{Δ_r} [sont des revêtements finis] … comme induits par D*_d → D*_Δ' (heavily crossed out, uncertain)
